issue.title: JSON: heap-buffer-overflow in encoder caused by indentation caching

labels.name: extension-modules
labels.description: C modules in the Modules dir

labels.name: type-crash
labels.description: A hard crash of the interpreter, possibly with a core dump

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: The issue has been accepted as valid by a triager.
pre-release feature fixes, bugs and security fixes

issue.body:
# Crash report

### What happened?

```python
import json

def bad_encoder1(*args):
    return None
enc = json.encoder.c_make_encoder(None, lambda obj: str(obj), bad_encoder1, r'\udcff', ': ', r'\udfff', False, -(2**64), False)    
enc({'spam': 10**1000}, 4)
```

comments.body:
On a debug build:
```
python: ./Modules/_json.c:1409: update_indent_cache: Assertion `indent_level * 2 == PyList_GET_SIZE(indent_cache) + 1' failed.
Aborted (core dumped)
```

Sligthly simplified version:
```python
from json.encoder import c_make_encoder
enc = c_make_encoder(None, str, str, '', ':', '', False, 1, False)
enc({'x': 'x'}, 1)
```

There's assertion crash on 3.14 and main, and no crash on 3.13.

On macOSX, Python 3.14, with the simplied example, the dump information seems to be more accurate.
